title: XSS prevention by output context
when: An app renders user supplied text into HTML on the server or in the browser, and each output context (text, attribute, URL, script data) must be encoded correctly.
prompt: Goal: Every place untrusted data reaches a page uses the encoder for its context, or a DOM API that needs none. Steps: 1. Browser: text through el.textContent, attributes through el.setAttribute (never on* names), lists built with createElement instead of HTML strings. 2. Server templates: one escapeHtml(s) mapping & < > " ' to & < > " ', applied by default; raw output needs an explicit raw() call that reviewers can grep. 3. Attributes are quoted and escaped; data never goes into on* attributes, style or srcdoc. 4. URLs: parse with new URL(value, location.origin) and allow only http: and https: before href or src, which blocks javascript: and data: links. 5. Data for scripts:

examples.input: usuarios conseguem colocar link javascript: no perfil
examples.output: protocol allowlist via new URL, escapeHtml by default in templates, JSON data island, payload tests
